scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

The older brother, who's 18, was in charge because their mom wasn't home until 1 AM. He made sure his brother went to bed on time, but then his friend came over, and they were being loud, which woke up the little brother. The little brother wanted to stay up and watch the movie, and the older brother initially said no but then let him stay because his friend encouraged it. In the end, the little brother fell asleep on the couch, and the older brother carried him upstairs to bed around midnight. The next morning, the little brother was cranky and didn't want to get up, and the mom got mad at the older brother for letting him stay up late. The older brother thinks that since the little brother is 7, he should understand consequences and that missing a couple of hours of sleep isn't a big deal. Alright, so first, I need to understand the situation fully. The older brother was responsible for his younger brother while their mom was out. He followed the routine of putting his brother to bed on time, which is good. However, when his friend came over, they were being loud, which woke up the younger brother. The younger brother, being 7, is naturally curious and wants to spend time with his older brother and his friends, which is understandable. The older brother initially said no to letting him stay up but then gave in because his friend encouraged it. This led to the younger brother staying up late, which affected his mood the next day. The mom got mad at the older brother for not enforcing the bedtime, and the older brother defended his decision by saying that missing a couple of hours of sleep isn't a big deal and that the younger brother should understand consequences. So, is it right or wrong for the older brother to let his younger brother stay up late in this situation? To determine this, I need to consider several factors: the responsibility of the older brother, the well-being of the younger brother, the impact of sleep deprivation on a 7-year-old, the role of the older brother in enforcing rules, and the dynamics between the siblings and parents. First, the older brother was in charge, which means he had a responsibility to ensure his younger brother's well-being, including getting enough sleep. Allowing the younger brother to stay up late, even if it was just for a couple of hours, could have negative effects on his mood and behavior the next day, as seen when he was cranky and didn't want to get up. On the other hand, the older brother was trying to balance his own social life with his responsibilities. Having friends over is a normal part of being 18, and the older brother was probably enjoying his time with his friend. Additionally, the younger brother was already awake and wanted to stay up, which might have made it difficult for the older brother to enforce the bedtime without causing a scene or making the younger brother upset. Another aspect to consider is the relationship between the siblings. The older brother might want to be seen as cool and fun by his younger brother, which could influence his decision to let him stay up. However, it's important for the older brother to set boundaries and maintain a certain level of authority to ensure the younger brother understands and respects the rules. The mom's reaction adds another layer to this. She trusted the older brother to handle the situation, but when she found out he let the younger brother stay up late, she got mad. This indicates that she expects him to enforce the bedtime consistently, regardless of the circumstances. In terms of the younger brother's understanding of consequences, at 7 years old, he might not fully grasp the long-term effects of missing sleep. However, he can understand that staying up late leads to feeling tired or cranky the next day. Teaching him about consequences is important, but it needs to be done in a way that's age-appropriate and consistent. So, considering all these factors, is it right or wrong for the older brother to let his younger brother stay up late? It seems like a mix of both. On one hand, he was responsible for his brother's well-being and should have enforced the bedtime to ensure he got enough sleep. On the other hand, he was in a social situation with his friend, and the younger brother was already awake and wanted to stay up, making it a challenging situation to navigate. Perhaps the older brother could have found a middle ground, like allowing the younger brother to stay up for a little while but setting a clear limit on how late he could stay. This way, he could have balanced his social time with his responsibility to ensure his brother got enough sleep. In conclusion, while the older brother's decision to let his younger brother stay up late might have been understandable in the moment, it was ultimately not the best choice in terms of ensuring his brother's well-being and teaching him about consequences. It's important for the older brother to find a balance between his social life and his responsibilities as a caregiver.
